question: A manager wants to know whether Claude's summary of a report she uploaded is faithful to it. What is the most reliable check?
options: A) Check that the summary's length is proportionate to the length of the original report.
B) Ask Claude to summarise the report again and see whether the two versions agree.
C) Read the summary's main claims against the relevant sections of the report itself.
D) Ask Claude to rate how faithful its own summary is to the report on a numerical scale.
correct_answers: C) Read the summary's main claims against the relevant sections of the report itself.
explanations: Incorrect. Proportion is unrelated to accuracy; a well-sized summary can still distort what the report says.
Incorrect. Two summaries can agree and both misrepresent the report, so agreement is not evidence of faithfulness.
Correct. The uploaded report is the standard the summary is meant to represent, so a direct comparison is the only check that can settle faithfulness.
Incorrect. A self-assigned score is generated in the same way as the summary and carries no independent weight.
